_source: readlink of GNU coreutils (debian:10, debian:12, debian:13, ubuntu:22.04, ubuntu:24.04, rockylinux:9, centos:7) and of BusyBox (busybox:1.25 = 1.25.1 uClibc, busybox:1.33 = 1.33.1 uClibc, busybox:1.36.1-musl), and a few texts of /proc, run with sh -c in containers of these images (docker run -d --rm --network none, one docker exec per case, cwd /tmp/w), 2026-10-22. Every case runs in /tmp/w as made once per container: a folder d, an empty file file, the links l1 -> file, l2 -> l1, dangling -> missing, dl -> d, abs -> /tmp/w/l2, loop1 -> loop2, loop2 -> loop1 and notdir -> file/x. Each case is [stdout, stderr, exit status]. Docker host linux/arm64 (Docker Desktop, kernel 7.0.14-linuxkit): every image ran as arm64 except busybox:1.25 (linux/amd64 only, emulated; its /proc/1/exe is the emulator's). LC_ALL as in the locale field (unset for BusyBox); rockylinux:9 has no en_US.UTF-8 without its langpack (no network), so it ran with C.UTF-8 (the quotes of gnulib's quote() are the same in both). The texts that name a PID (/proc/self, /etc/mtab -f) and the times of ls -l are those of the run. applets: busybox --list | grep -x readlink and the banner of the image. proc: /proc/1 is the container's sleep, /proc/self the reading program. A second run on the same images and digests (2026-10-22, the same setup) added the cases of a name with a slash at its end: readlink -f / -m / -e missing/, -f d/missing/, -f file/, -f dangling/. A third run on the same images and digests (2026-10-22) added -f of a missing name followed by a dot or two slashes: readlink -f missing/., missing/./, missing// and the case d/missing/. (the dot belongs to the case name, the period after it ends the sentence).
